items.title: 71231_Sam Wooding Oral History Interview
items.q: We went out there and worked for a man called "Bony" Allen.

ctx.x: Well, Jimmy Harrison was from Detroit. And so was Fats. And they built up this great picture, how things was going to be out there, and you could walk down the street and pick up a hundred dollars in the street, see. And they had everything there, but there wasn't no mines in town, but it was almost as bad as the gold miners.

So we went out there and we did alright. We went out there and worked for a man called "Bony" Allen. And this man had a cabaret, but he was in bad health and he had to go to Hot Springs for his health. And he had -- he owed us about two thousand dollars, or fifteen hundred dollars, I guess, for the band. Because he was half sick, so he said, "Boys, I ain't got any money, but I've got a cabaret here and I've got to go away.
